correctness_confidence.basis: All proofs in Theorems 1-3 are mathematically sound, from the antipodal spherical-cap stability estimate and d-dimensional telescoping/John rigidity to the zonotope shadow-boundary characterization and exact polyhedral evaluations across all 11 canonical bodies.

novelty.basis: The paper contributes original quantitative stability bounds for AHZ cube rigidity, a clean Universal Zero-Variance Zonotope Theorem, sharp d-dimensional extensions, exact Minkowski-over-Euclidean regime jumps on canonical bodies, and the exact epsilon-cube transition.

reproducibility.basis: Reproducibility is exceptional: 20 dependency-free Lean 4.36.0 theorems compile cleanly under -DwarningAsError=true with zero sorry or Classical.choice, alongside an AST-audited zero-float rational interval verifier, 16 SHA-256 certificates, and 56 passing pytest checks.

rigor.basis: The analytical arguments are complete and exact, every canonical 3D polytope is verified in exact John position with outward-rounded rational brackets narrower than 1e-8, and all boundary cases such as L_S = 2 and epsilon = 1/2 are handled without gaps.

significance.basis: These results sharpen the quantitative foundations of the AHZ proof of 3D Hadwiger's conjecture, clarify where Euclidean mean-width bounds lose to Minkowski shadow lengths, and establish sharp barriers for higher-dimensional generalizations.

summary: This paper provides a thorough quantitative and structural analysis of the Aiger-Har-Peled-Zuzic (AHZ) proof of Hadwiger's covering conjecture in R^3. Theorem 1 upgrades AHZ's qualitative cube rigidity to an explicit stability inequality eta(K) >= d_H(S_tilde, Z)^3 / 9 via two disjoint antipodal spherical caps, giving explicit shadow-boundary homothety factors strictly below 1 for non-parallelepipeds, and extends both Lemma 3.4 (threshold L_S < 2) and Theorem 5.3 (mean-width bound d*kappa_d with parallelepiped rigidity) to all dimensions d >= 2. Theorem 2 establishes the covering ladder 8 int h_{S_tilde} < 2m => c(K) <= 2 + m and computes exact Euclidean and Minkowski Lemma 6.4(iii) shadow lengths across eleven canonical 3D bodies, proving strict Minkowski regime jumps for the octahedron (c <= 7), tetrahedron and cuboctahedron (c <= 6), and unit ball (4/pi zig-zagging gap, c <= 6), plus a dodecahedron-icosahedron ordering reversal. Theorem 3 proves unconditional sharpness of L_S < 2 in all dimensions, establishes a Universal Zero-Variance Zonotope Theorem (L_Z === 4 sum ||z_i||_Z), and locates the exact epsilon-rounded cube jump at epsilon > 1/2. All algebraic claims and interval bounds pass independent Lean 4.36.0 and 56 zero-float pytest checks.
strengths: Clean, elementary, and fully explicit quantitative cube-rigidity stability bound eta(K) >= d_H(S_tilde, Z)^3 / 9 with exact spherical-cap disjointness and John contact-defect lower bound.

Universal Zero-Variance Zonotope Theorem (Theorem 3(b)) giving a unified closed form L_Z(Sigma(Z, w)) === 4 sum ||z_i||_Z identically for every generic direction w in G(Z) and explaining why directional optimization fails for the cube, hexagonal prism, rhombic dodecahedron, and truncated octahedron.

Exact, closed-form evaluations of both Euclidean mean-width bounds and Minkowski Lemma 6.4(iii) shadow lengths across eleven canonical 3D convex bodies, revealing strict regime jumps and the dodecahedron-icosahedron ordering reversal.
Rigorous d-dimensional extensions of Lemma 3.4 and Theorem 5.3 with exact Gamma/Wallis constants and unconditional L_S < 2 sharpness.
Outstanding verification suite: 20 dependency-free, axiom-pure Lean 4.36.0 theorems, zero-float pure-integer rational interval certificates to < 1e-8, and 56 passing adversarial tests.
weaknesses: The Lean 4.36.0 suite formalizes the discrete algebraic, arithmetic, and inductive telescoping cores rather than full Mathlib measure-theoretic integration on S^2, John's theorem, or Helly's theorem.

In the proof of Eq. (3) (Theorem 1(a)), the passage from polyhedral approximation to L_S(gamma_{w_*}) <= 12 - eta(K) for general non-polytopes glosses over an arbitrarily small approximation slack (which the stated 1 - eta(K)/24 bound and parenthetical infimum nevertheless absorb rigorously).

While Theorem 3(c) shows linear scaling eta(K_eps) ~ d_H(K_eps, Z) for global rounding, the manuscript does not discuss whether the cubic exponent 3 in Theorem 1(a) is tight for localized vertex truncations of the cube.
strong_novelty_candidates: Quantitative cube-rigidity stability inequality eta(K) >= d_H(S_tilde, Z)^3 / 9 and explicit shadow-boundary homothety bound lambda_Sigma <= max(1/2, 1 - d_H(S_tilde, Z)^3 / 216).
Universal Zero-Variance Zonotope Theorem proving L_Z(Sigma(Z, w)) === 4 sum ||z_i||_Z identically for every generic direction w in G(Z).
Exact Minkowski-over-Euclidean covering regime jumps (octahedron c <= 7; tetrahedron, cuboctahedron, and ball c <= 6 with 4/pi outer-polytope gap) and dodecahedron-icosahedron ordering reversal.
Sharp linear mean-width transition 8 int h_{K_eps} = 12 - 4*eps with c <= 8 -> c <= 7 jump at eps > 1/2.
